subject: Human Evolution
title: The Foramen Magnum Shift
description: A short lesson to help you apply The Foramen Magnum Shift.

hook.text: The hole where the spine enters the skull moved from the back to the bottom. That shift is key evidence.

buildup.text: In quadrupeds, the foramen magnum faces backward so the head looks forward while on all fours.

discovery.text: In bipeds, it faces downward, balancing the skull directly on top of the vertical spine.

twist.text: This simple measurement on a skull fragment can reveal whether a species walked upright—even without legs.

climax.text: Toumaï's foramen magnum position is why some scientists call it a biped despite having no leg bones.

punchline.text: A hole in the skull tells how the body moved.

quiz.question: Where is the foramen magnum in bipedal species?
options: At the back of the skull
At the base of the skull
At the top of the skull
